can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of common adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: additive stacking of attributes
ontology.pedagogical_hook: add another brushstroke

negatives: He opened the door and walked in.
positives: The teachers are very nice and friendly.
It is big and comfortable.

can_do_statement: Can use 'very' with a limited range of common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: very pushes the attribute up the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: turn it up

negatives: Thank you very much for your help.
positives: I like Croydon because it's very quiet and very nice.
My neighbours are very friendly.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives attributively, before a noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: ATTRIBUTIVE_PLACEMENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: determiner + adjective + noun — slot the adjective before its noun as a foreground modifier
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker foregrounds a property directly on the entity

positives: We have a big garden and a small swimming pool.
My name is Bogdan. I am your new neighbour.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives predicatively, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: basic attribute delivery after be
ontology.pedagogical_hook: be then the word

positives: My bedroom is big.
This place is lovely.

can_do_statement: Can use the irregular superlative adjective 'best' in the phrase 'my best friend'.

ontology.mental_model: one person crowned as top member of a set by the speaker
ontology.pedagogical_hook: crown your number-one person
ontology.agency_or_distance: possessive anchors the ranking to the speaker's own world

positives: She's my best friend.
Marco has been my best friend since primary school.
negatives: I always try to do my best.
This is the best pizza in town.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'soon' in the phrases 'See you soon' and 'Get well soon', as a signing-off device.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_CLOSING_ANCHOR
ontology.pedagogical_hook: see you / get well + soon — closes the conversation with a forward-pointing adverb
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker hands the hearer a near-future expectation as a parting signal

positives: See you soon.
Get well soon.
negatives: I will come back soon after lunch.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('here', 'there') to indicate place.

ontology.mental_model: LOCATIVE_STAGING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: here / there — point to a place on the conversational stage
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker deictically anchors an entity in shared space

positives: My girlfriend is here with me.
I was born there and I lived there over twenty years.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'really' and 'very much' with verbs expressing preference ('like', 'love'), for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: AMPLIFIED_PREFERENCE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: really / very much + like/love — turn the dial past the standard setting
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks the affective state as more than ordinary

positives: I really like theatre and classical music.
I really love my space!
negatives: I would like to go home.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'very' to make adjectives stronger.

ontology.mental_model: DEGREE_AMPLIFIER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: very + adjective — push the adjective past its default setting
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker escalates the force of a quality word

positives: He's a very good man.
I'm very happy in my home.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('always', 'sometimes') to talk about frequency.

ontology.mental_model: FREQUENCY_INDEXICAL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: always / sometimes — place the event on a frequency dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the event on the spectrum from never-to-always

positives: I like Dorchester's people, they are always very friendly and polite.
I always see Safora because she lives near my home.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs in front position.

ontology.mental_model: CLAUSE_HEAD_PLACEMENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Sometimes / Often / Yesterday / Tomorrow — slot the adverb at the head of the clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker opens the clause with a framing adverb

positives: Sometimes I go to the beach.
Tomorrow I will see her at the airport.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs before an adjective.

ontology.mental_model: DEGREE_PRE_ADJACENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: very / really / quite + adjective — slot the intensifier just before the adjective
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker intensifies the adjective from a zero position

positives: My home is very light and very comfortable.
I have a really good friend, her name is Dylma.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use frequency adverbs in the usual mid position, between the subject and the main verb.

ontology.mental_model: MEDIAL_FREQUENCY_SLOT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + always/usually/often/sometimes + verb — slot the adverb between subject and verb
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks the verb's frequency medially

positives: I always listen to music in my free time.
She often goes to the park with her dog.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'really' in the usual mid-position, between the subject and the main verb.

ontology.mental_model: MID_INTENSIFIER_SLOT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + really + verb — slot the intensifier between subject and main verb

positives: I really love walking in the park.
I really like my kitchen because it is big.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use time adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.mental_model: FINAL_TIME_ANCHOR
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + yesterday/today/tomorrow/soon/now/just/already — anchor the time at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker places the time at the end of the clause

positives: I hope to see you soon.
She went to the park yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use place adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.mental_model: FINAL_LOCATIVE_ANCHOR
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + here/there/nearby/abroad/away/upstairs/downstairs — anchor the place at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates entities at the end of the clause

positives: I have many friends there.
My parents live there.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can modify adverbs of time and degree with 'very'.

ontology.mental_model: Scaling temporal or degree adverbs to high intensity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Modifying simple adverbs of time and degree with 'very'

positives: I hope you will be fine very soon.
I like my job very much.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in a limited range of contexts to refer to places from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific place or thing.

positives: I want to let you know about this area.
I like this place because there are many cultures.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with time and date words to refer to 'the one that's coming'.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of future temporal points or periods.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'this' upcoming event or time.

positives: This summer I want to go on holiday.
I have a good plan for this weekend.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with singular nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item.

positives: I like this place because it is very nice.
If you like, then we can go this Saturday.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiners 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her' and 'our' before nouns. ► noun phrases ► possessive pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: I live with my family.
She lost her favorite book.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('some', 'lots of', 'a lot of' and numbers).

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: Near my home there are some shops.
My house has got three rooms.
negatives: I have a lot of water.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('a', 'every').► determiners: articles

ontology.mental_model: Singling out a specific countable entity or referring to all instances distributively.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a' for one thing or 'every' for all things of that type.

positives: I go to college every day.
I have a big kitchen in my house.
negatives: I go to college all days.
I have big kitchens in my house.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.

ontology.mental_model: Basic action-target linkage
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Verbs like 'listen' always take 'to' when indicating what is heard.

positives: I listen to music in the living room.
I can look after her if she needs.
negatives: I can look around the house today.
They asked me a quick question.

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary verb 'be'. ►  present continuous

ontology.mental_model: In-progress temporal anchoring
ontology.pedagogical_hook: The 'be' verb helps mark the action as happening right now.

positives: I am writing to tell you what I do every day.
We are going to the park.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there is' + singular noun phrase as complement.

ontology.mental_model: Existential assertion of singularity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'There is' introduces the existence of one thing.

positives: My home is nice, there is a nice garden.
In my home there's a kitchen.
negatives: There are two bedrooms in my house.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there are' + plural noun phrase as complement.

ontology.mental_model: Existential assertion of plurality
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'There are' introduces the existence of multiple things.

positives: There are two bathrooms in my apartment.
I think, in the park there are animals.
negatives: There is a nice garden outside.
There were many people at the party.

can_do_statement: Can use 'but' to join a limited range of common adjectives, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: contrastive layering of attributes on one entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: paint then correct the picture

negatives: He bought milk but forgot eggs.
She is a teacher but works late.
positives: The weather was cloudy but fine.
It was cheap but beautiful.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of two syllables ending in '-y' by changing the 'y' to an 'I' and adding '-er'.

ontology.mental_model: y-roots shift spelling on the comparison scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: y becomes i on the ladder

negatives: He is taller and stronger than before.
It was better than the first one.
positives: It is small and easier to use than other phones.
The students were happier and there were lots of stories.

can_do_statement: Can use comparative adjectives attributively, before nouns.

ontology.mental_model: comparison glued to the noun it ranks
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the ranked noun

positives: I watched a cricket match with my younger brother.
I want to get a better job in the city.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives from adjectives of one syllable by adding '-er'.

ontology.mental_model: one-syllable roots take the bare -er suffix
ontology.pedagogical_hook: short word, add er

positives: I played computer games with my older brother.
The shirt was cheaper than the trousers.

can_do_statement: Can form a range of comparative adjective phrases using 'more' + longer adjectives (usually three or more syllables).

ontology.mental_model: long roots outsource comparison to 'more'
ontology.pedagogical_hook: long word? let more do the work

positives: I think you must be more careful.
It was more expensive than the other clothes.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable ending in 'e', by adding '-r'.

ontology.mental_model: silent e stays, r attaches directly
ontology.pedagogical_hook: e already there, just add r

positives: I think it will be nicer.
It is safer to come by aeroplane.

can_do_statement: Can use comparative adjectives as a complement of 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: be hands the subject its position on the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: be + the scale point

positives: It would be better if you came after 4.30.
You can come by bus, it's easier.

can_do_statement: Can form irregular comparative adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: root swaps entirely on the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the word jumps the ladder

positives: What colour do you think is better?
For further information, contact us.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable with a short vowel, by doubling the final consonant and adding '-er'

ontology.mental_model: short vowel locks the consonant before -er
ontology.pedagogical_hook: double it, then er

negatives: This shirt is cheaper than that one.
positives: I prefer my room because it is bigger.
The weather is getting hotter.

can_do_statement: Can use a comparative adjective with 'than' to compare two nouns or noun phrases.► comparative clauses

ontology.mental_model: than names the rival scale point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: name the rival

negatives: Other than that, it was fine.
We would rather stay home tonight.
positives: It's smaller than my old phone.
The weather in Thailand was hotter than in Vietnam.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' with common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: the scale tips past the usable point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: over the limit

negatives: It took two hours to finish.
positives: They aren't too expensive.
The other one that I had was too small.

can_do_statement: Can form adjective phrases with a very limited range of adjectives + a prepositional phrase.

ontology.mental_model: the attribute points at a location or target
ontology.pedagogical_hook: point the adjective

negatives: He is a good man at heart.
positives: I think swimming is good for my body.
The house was full of people.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' + adjective + prepositional phrase

ontology.mental_model: excess measured against a person or thing
ontology.pedagogical_hook: too much, for whom?

negatives: That box is small for a reason.
positives: Most of my clothes were too small for me.
The shoes were too tight for her feet.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs of degree ('really', 'so', 'quite') with an increasing range of common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: really, so, quite set different volume levels
ontology.pedagogical_hook: pick the volume

negatives: So, what did he say about the plan?
positives: It was sunny and really hot every day!
They are quite expensive.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives ('main', 'only') that limit the noun that they go before.

ontology.mental_model: limiter fences the noun down to one
ontology.pedagogical_hook: fence the noun

positives: The main reason is that I am practising the language.
The only thing that I didn't like was the weather.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adjectives predicatively, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: be hands the attribute to the subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: say it after be

detection.regex_triage: \b(?:i am|you are|he is|she is|it is|we are|they are|i was|you were|he was|she was|it was|we were|they were)\s+(free|friendly|happy|tired|ready|busy|kind|lovely|beautiful|nice)\b

positives: Yes, I am free on Monday morning.
I love her because she is friendly.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives predicatively, after linking verbs 'look' and 'feel'.

ontology.mental_model: look and feel pipe the attribute through the senses
ontology.pedagogical_hook: sense it, then say it

negatives: I feel the heat of the sun.
positives: It is black and it looks perfect.
I feel comfortable when I am wearing these clothes.

can_do_statement: Can form a limited range of complex noun phrases with a superlative adjective  + prepositional phrase, to talk about something unique.► noun phrases ►  clauses: comparison

ontology.mental_model: a superlative plus a set-specifier phrase carves out the single unique member
ontology.pedagogical_hook: name the thing, then name the world it beats
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions an entity as one-of-everything

positives: It is the biggest zoo in the world.
They were the happiest days of my life.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of prepositional phrases with 'of' after a superlative adjective, to refer to one thing within a set or part of a set.

ontology.mental_model: 'of' names the set from which the ranked member is drawn
ontology.pedagogical_hook: best of WHAT? - of names the pile
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker picks one thing out of a stated set

positives: My teacher said that it was the best project of all.
I learned to surf, this was the best part of the trip.
negatives: It's the biggest room in the house.
It was the best day ever.

can_do_statement: Can use prepositional phrases with 'in' + singular name of a place after a superlative adjective.

ontology.mental_model: 'in' names the spatial container that bounds the comparison set
ontology.pedagogical_hook: biggest WHERE? - in names the place
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the top-ranked thing inside a place

positives: It's the biggest room in the house.
I bought them because they are the cheapest clothes in the shop.
negatives: You will miss the best party of the year!
The keys are in the house.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the '-est' suffix, with adjectives of one syllable, and with two-syllable adjectives ending in -y.

ontology.mental_model: the -est / -iest suffix stamps a word as rank-one on a scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: y becomes i before you crown it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades things to the top rung

positives: The easiest way to get to my house is by Underground.
You are the funniest person that I have ever seen!
negatives: This phone is bigger than my old one.
It's the most comfortable chair in the house.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'my' or 'your' + superlative adjective + noun, with a limited range of nouns and contexts. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: a possessive determiner hands the top rank to a person
ontology.pedagogical_hook: my + the-most-thing + noun
ontology.agency_or_distance: possessive ties the superlative to an involved party

positives: I bought these clothes for my youngest brother.
Please wear your oldest clothes.
negatives: My brother is the oldest in our family.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable with a short vowel, by doubling the final consonant and adding '–est'.

ontology.mental_model: short-vowel words double their last consonant before taking the crown
ontology.pedagogical_hook: big -> bigger -> the BIGGEST - hold the consonant
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks top rank with doubled-consonant spelling

positives: It's the biggest and oldest museum in Libya.
Today was the hottest day of the entire summer.
negatives: It was the cheapest in this shop!
She's the funniest person I know.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'the' + superlative adjective + noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: 'the' plus a -est adjective flags exactly one noun as peak of its kind
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the + -est + thing
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker presents the ranking as given, unique

positives: It has the latest technology.
The best place to visit is La Baule.
negatives: My youngest brother helped me with the boxes.
The zoo was big and the aquarium was bigger.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the suffix '-st' to adjectives ending in '–e'.

ontology.mental_model: words already ending in e just add -st to reach top rank
ontology.pedagogical_hook: late -> the latest: keep the e, add -st
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades to the extreme using e-final stems

positives: I always watch the latest music videos from there.
But the nicest thing at my party was my presents.
negatives: It's the biggest room in the house.
He was the tallest player on the team.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives by adding the suffix '-est', to adjectives of one syllable.

ontology.mental_model: a one-syllable adjective bolts -est on the end to claim top rank
ontology.pedagogical_hook: old, older, the OLD - est
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker asserts an absolute peak on a scale

positives: It was the cheapest in this shop!
He is the oldest of the three brothers.
negatives: The easiest way to get to my house is by Underground.
You are the funniest person that I have ever seen!

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjective phrases using 'the most', with longer adjectives of two or more syllables.

ontology.mental_model: TWO_SYLLABLE_STAMP
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the most + adjective — stamp a multi-syllable adjective as rank-one
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades two-plus-syllable adjectives to the top

positives: That was the most delicious meal I have ever eaten.
This is the most interesting book in the library.
negatives: I am most grateful for your help.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('so much', 'a lot') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity. ► determiners

ontology.mental_model: INTENSITY_VOCALISATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: so much / a lot — amplify the verb to maximum volume
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker cranks the speaker-level of feeling or action

positives: I am looking forward to seeing you so much!
We listened to music and we danced a lot too.
negatives: He is so kind to me.
I love you more than anything.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('also', 'so', 'however') to show a relationship between two clauses or sentences.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_COUPLING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: also / so / however — wire two ideas into one discourse
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker binds clauses into a relationship of addition, result, or contrast

positives: I also bought some t-shirts.
I don't like green, so I decided to use blue.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('yesterday', 'just', 'now', 'already',) to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.mental_model: DEICTIC_TIME_ANCHOR
ontology.pedagogical_hook: yesterday / just / now / already — pin the event to a point on the speech-time line
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker anchors the event relative to S

positives: Yesterday I went shopping.
I've just seen your mail.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of manner adverbs and adverb phrases to modify how something happens.

ontology.mental_model: MANNER_QUALIFICATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: well / straight / slowly — describe HOW the action is performed
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker sculpts the texture of the verb's action

positives: Both the players played well.
You must go straight, then turn left.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('usually', 'often', 'never', 'weekly') to talk about frequency.

ontology.mental_model: FREQUENCY_GRADIENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: usually / often / never / weekly — finer-grained frequency markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions the event on a denser frequency scale

positives: People usually try to eat their breakfast between 7 and 9 am.
I have to pay weekly or monthly?

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs ('so', 'quite', 'too') to modify adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: DEGREE_CALIBRATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: so / quite / too + adjective — turn the adjective up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker sets the adjective's intensity on a non-default position

positives: It's so beautiful.
It was quite expensive, it cost one hundred pounds.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('only', 'just') to focus on or point to something.

ontology.mental_model: FOCUS_NARROWING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: only / just — spotlight a single element, dimming the rest
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent from a presumed larger set

positives: It's only two hours.
I have only one chance.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('first', 'then', 'after that') to order segments of discourse.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_LINEARISATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: first / then / after that — map the events onto a timeline
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker arranges discourse events in chronological order

positives: First we had a dinner, then we went to a disco.
Add the eggs, then stir for two minutes.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('actually', 'unfortunately', 'of course', 'I’m sorry') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.mental_model: REFINED_STANCE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: simply / truly / surely / apparently / naturally / surprisingly / inevitably — finer-grained stance markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks nuanced distance from the proposition

positives: Obviously everybody has the right to be on a strike.
We can't truly blame ourselves.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('maybe', 'perhaps') to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.mental_model: CERTAINTY_GRADIENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — finer-grained certainty markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: And it will probably be on TV next month!
If I were you I'd certainly choose not to go.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use manner adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.mental_model: FINAL_MANNER_QUALIFICATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + well/quickly/slowly/loudly — slot the manner adverb at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker describes how the action was performed at the end

positives: Please answer me quickly because there are only eleven tickets.
She drives carefully on icy roads.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs in mid position between the subject and the main verb and after modal verbs, auxiliary verbs and 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: MEDIAL_ADVERB_SLOT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + can/will/be + adverb + main verb — slot the adverb after aux/modal/be
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker places the adverb in the medial slot

positives: I have always loved reading novels.
She is probably going to arrive late.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs before an adjective.

ontology.mental_model: DEGREE_PRE_ADJACENT_WIDE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: so / quite / too + adjective — turn the adjective to a non-default intensity

positives: I'm so glad you are coming.
They are quite expensive.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs in front position.

ontology.mental_model: CLAUSE_HEAD_PLACEMENT_WIDE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: However / Furthermore / Moreover / Actually — slot a wider set of adverbials at the clause head
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker opens the clause with a wider set of framing adverbials

positives: However I can study only on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.
Furthermore, the cost is much lower this year.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use degree adverbs in end position.

ontology.mental_model: FINAL_DEGREE_AMPLIFICATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + a lot / so much / very much — push the degree to the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker amplifies degree at the end of the clause

positives: I miss you a lot.
I am looking forward to seeing you so much!
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use evaluative, viewpoint and sequencing adverbs outside the clause, in front position, as a cohesive device to link to a previous statement in a preceding clause.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_HEAD_HOOK
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Actually / However / Fortunately / Interestingly / In addition — fronted adverbs as cohesion hooks
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker head-loads a discourse link into the next clause

positives: Actually I want you to decide what colour my room should be.
Fortunately, the train was on time that morning.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can modify a limited range of adverbs of time, degree, and manner with other adverbs.

ontology.mental_model: Refining the temporal or manner frame of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combining basic adverbs for precise time or degree

positives: I love it so much.
I really need it right now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be' + 'like' + noun or pronoun.

ontology.mental_model: Similitude
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing identity or form

positives: I like her because she is like me.
It's like a little train.

can_do_statement: Can form an affirmative imperative with the base form of a main verb.

positives: Bring your swim-suit for the swimming pool.
Call me if you need anything.
negatives: You bring your swim-suit every day.
Calling me was a big mistake.

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to give instructions.

ontology.mental_model: DIRECT_ACTION_CONTROL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Route Script — issuing sequenced commands that walk the listener through a procedure or a journey.

positives: Take a taxi to the station then call me.
Walk a little bit more and then change to line 8.
negatives: He then changed his mind and took a taxi.
I will take a taxi to the airport tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use negative imperative after an instruction, for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: DIRECT_ACTION_CONTROL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Second Nail — driving the warning home after the instruction has already landed.

positives: Don't forget!
Don't be late!

can_do_statement: Can use 'let's' + base form of a main verb, for first person plural imperatives to make a suggestion.

positives: Let's go to the town centre, it is an interesting place.
Let's meet at half past four.
negatives: He lets us go home early.
Let us not forget our bags.

can_do_statement: Can form a negative imperative with the auxiliary verb 'do' + 'n't' + base form of a main verb, to give advice, instructions or orders.

positives: Don't tell Lucy, please.
Don't worry, I'll be there.
negatives: I don't think you should leave.

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to give instructions, often at the end of a letter or when saying goodbye to someone.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_COHESION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Channel Keep-Alive — closing the letter with an action-token that holds the connection open.

positives: Write to me soon.
Call me back.
negatives: Take care of the garden for me.
I will call you back later.

can_do_statement: Can use 'What a pity' + ('that') clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing regret or disappointment over a situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'what a pity' followed by a clause to express feelings.

positives: What a pity that you couldn't make it.
What a pity it rained all day.
negatives: She felt pity for the poor dog.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying a specific thing.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' as the subject in a defining relative clause.

positives: I want a car which runs fast.
He read a book which changed his life.
negatives: The house, which is red, is nice.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject,.

ontology.mental_model: Adding extra, non-essential information about a thing.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' in a non-defining relative clause.

positives: My car, which is red, is very fast.
I read that book, which was very interesting.
negatives: The car which I bought is red.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with uncountable nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular, or uncountable entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or substance.

positives: I found this information in a book.
My mother told me that this food is healthy.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' with singular nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'that' specific item.

positives: I also want to see that film.
I know we have that course in our college.
negatives: I also want to see this film.
I know we have these courses.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' to talk about or point to things which are further away in time and space from the speaker or writer

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'that' specific item or place.

positives: Look at that building over there.
I remember that day clearly.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' to refer to something with immediate relevance which has already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities with immediate relevance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'this' specific thing just discussed.

positives: We discussed the issue. Let's focus on this problem.
She bought a dress. The colour of this dress is beautiful.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in an increasing range of contexts to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ► pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or place.

positives: I am writing this letter to you.
You can contact me on this number.
negatives: You can contact me on that number.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in an increasing range of contexts to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ► pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or place.

positives: I am writing this letter to tell you about my present.
You can contact me by calling me this number.
negatives: You can contact me on that number.

can_do_statement: Can use 'these' with plural nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, plural entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'these' specific items.

positives: I bought these clothes because they weren't expensive.
I bought these things because they were perfect.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' to refer to something which has already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'that' specific thing previously mentioned.

positives: You should go that shop.
I want to study that course.
negatives: I want to study this course.

can_do_statement: Can use 'these' to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, plural entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'these' specific items or places.

positives: I like these restaurants in the city.
These books are very interesting.

can_do_statement: Can use 'those' to refer to things which have already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'those' specific things previously mentioned.

positives: I bought those clothes because I'm going to Japan.
It is black and pink, I like those colours very much.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' after singular or proper nouns to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: I found my sister's jacket.
We are going to Linda's party.

can_do_statement: Can use quantifying determiners + possessive determiners + 'of' + noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: All of my friends were there.
Bring some of your DVDs.

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in negative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying uncountable entities in absence or low quantity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not much' to describe a small amount of something you can't count.

positives: We didn't have much money for the trip.
I haven't got much time to watch television.
negatives: We had much money for the trip.
She hasn't seen many friends lately.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('each', 'an', 'one' and numbers).

ontology.mental_model: Specifying exact quantities or individual components of a group.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'each', 'an', 'one', or numbers to talk about single items.

positives: Each class is about one hour long.
We have an extra ticket for the concert.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners ('some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of') with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing indefinite quantities for both countable and uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of' for things you have many of, or can't count.

positives: I think we should bring some water.
There were no clouds in the sky.
negatives: I think we should bring a bottle.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('all', 'both', 'a few').

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying plural entities as totalities or small subsets.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all', 'both', or 'a few' to talk about multiple things.

positives: This notice is for all students.
I'm just writing to tell you a few things.
negatives: This notice is for every student.
I'm just writing to tell you one thing.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so many' and 'too many' with plural nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so many' or 'too many' to exaggerate a lot of things.

positives: We played so many games together.
I know I bought too many things.
negatives: I know I bought too much food.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', number + 'of', 'each of'). ► pronouns: quantity

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', or numbers with 'of the' or 'of my'.

positives: I spent all of my money!
Some of my friends gave me books.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there is' + uncountable nouns as complement.

ontology.mental_model: Existential assertion of mass
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Uncountable nouns use singular 'there is'.

positives: I need it because there is some money in it.
There is some information about the new art class.
negatives: There is a dog sleeping on the floor.
There's a lot of people here.

can_do_statement: Can use both 'there is' and 'there are' + 'a lot of' + plural noun.

ontology.mental_model: Existential assertion of abundance
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'a lot of' to state there is a large quantity of something.

positives: There's a lot of people there.
You can go to the town centre because there are a lot of shops.
negatives: There are many people standing around.
There is one person who can help.

guideword: FORM: COMBINING MORE THAN TWO ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can use commas and 'and' to join more than two adjectives, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: list of attributes closed by and
ontology.pedagogical_hook: list them, then close the list

positives: She is beautiful, intelligent, funny and reliable.
He is tall, thin and friendly.

guideword: FORM: COMBINING THE SAME COMPARATIVE ADJECTIVE WITH 'AND'
can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to repeat a comparative adjective to indicate change over time, usually after 'become' or get. ► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.mental_model: same scale intensifying over time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the change keeps changing

positives: The room became hotter and hotter.
The weather got colder and colder.

can_do_statement: Can use a comma to combine two adjectives used before the noun, following the usual order of adjective types.

ontology.mental_model: stack attributes before the noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: load the noun

positives: Its huge, black screen was impressive.
They bought a big, red car yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of compound adjectives ('good-looking', 'well-known')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen joins two roots into one trait
ontology.pedagogical_hook: two roots, one trait

positives: He is good-looking.
She is well-known.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of comparative adjectives.► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.mental_model: two scales raised together
ontology.pedagogical_hook: more of both

positives: He is taller and stronger than before.
This car is cheaper and faster.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to repeat a comparative adjective to indicate change over time, usually after 'become' or 'get'.  ► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.mental_model: same scale intensifying over time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the change keeps changing

negatives: The team is bigger and stronger than last year.
positives: I saw everything become smaller and smaller.
Nowadays television is getting worse and worse.

can_do_statement: Can use '(so) much' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: much stretches the distance between two scale points
ontology.pedagogical_hook: widen the gap

negatives: There was much more time last year.
positives: The teacher in the new class is much better than the last one.
The house is so much bigger than the previous one.

can_do_statement: Can use 'a (little) bit' to modify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: a bit narrows the distance between scale points
ontology.pedagogical_hook: shrink the gap politely

negatives: He is a big brother to me.
positives: He's a bit smaller than me, dark hair.
She's a little bit older than me.

can_do_statement: Can use 'even' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be' and 'get'.

ontology.mental_model: even pushes an already high point higher
ontology.pedagogical_hook: climb one rung more

positives: Part two was even better!
My smile got even bigger.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' before adjectives followed by 'to'-infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: excess degree slams the door on the action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: too much, so it can't happen

negatives: He is too busy for hobbies.
positives: He was too busy to write a letter to me.
The machine is too old to work well.

can_do_statement: Can use 'enough' to modify adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: the attribute reaches the threshold
ontology.pedagogical_hook: past the line

negatives: We have enough money for the trip.
positives: My room is big enough, there is a lot of space.
We don't think our English is good enough.

can_do_statement: Can use adjective phrases attributively, before a noun.

ontology.mental_model: intensifier plus adjective packed before the noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: stack it before the noun

positives: I have a very important meeting at 10.15 am.
She's also a really good friend.

can_do_statement: Can form adjective phrases with 'quite a' + adjective.

ontology.mental_model: quite a lifts the whole noun phrase a notch
ontology.pedagogical_hook: quite a step up

positives: I have been thinking about it for quite a long time.
This is quite a difficult situation you have.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives with the prefix a- ('asleep', 'awake', 'alive', 'alone') predicatively only, after linking verbs.

ontology.mental_model: a- adjectives are states, never glued before nouns
ontology.pedagogical_hook: a- words stay after the verb

negatives: I live alone in a small flat.
The alive topic was on the news.
positives: I was very nervous because I was alone at the bus station.
My father was still alive.

can_do_statement:
Can use an increasing range of adjectives attributively, before a noun.
► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: several attributes stack inside the noun phrase
ontology.pedagogical_hook: stack them in order

negatives: The character is main to the plot.
Her hair is long and dark.
positives: The main character in the programme is a journalist.
He had long dark hair and a short fair beard.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives as object complement after 'make'.

ontology.mental_model: RESULT_STATE_NAMING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: make + object + adjective — name the result state of the action on the entity
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker attributes the resulting state to a caused entity

positives: That makes me angry!
She made the room beautiful with fresh flowers.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use an adjective or adjective phrase after pronouns like 'something', 'nothing', 'somewhere', 'nowhere'.

ontology.mental_model: INDETERMINATE_PLACEMENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: something / nothing + adjective — leave the referent vague and color it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker keeps the referent indeterminate while coloring it

positives: I want to cook something special for dinner tonight.
But something terrible happened that morning.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with a superlative adjective + prepositional phrase, to talk about something unique. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Situating a superlative within a defined scope or domain via prepositions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming complex superlative noun phrases for precise uniqueness

positives: Yesterday was the most exciting day of my life!
Exercise is undoubtedly the most important thing in our lives.
negatives: It was a very exciting day of my life.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'THE BEST' WITH NOUN AND PRESENT PERFECT
can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' before a noun + present perfect to talk about a unique experience.

ontology.mental_model: UNIQUE_EXPERIENCE_REICHENBACH
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the best + noun + have ever + past participle — name a unique experience up to speech time
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the unique experience at the open-ended present

positives: It's the best meal I have ever eaten.
That was the best trip we have ever taken.
negatives: It was the best meal yesterday.
The best thing about her is her honesty.

guideword: FORM: 'THE BEST' WITH NOUN AND  'TO-' INFINITIVE
can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' before a noun + 'to'-infinitive.  ► clauses: comparative

ontology.mental_model: TOP_CONTEXT_FOR_INFINITIVE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the best + noun + to + verb — name the top context for an action
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions an action as the top-of-its-kind purpose

positives: It's the best time to visit the city.
That's the best way to learn English.
negatives: It's the best meal in the city.
That was the best movie we saw.

can_do_statement: Can use 'one of the' before a superlative adjective, followed by a plural noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Positioning an entity within a top-tier group rather than as an absolute singular
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'one of the' for inclusive superlatives

positives: It was one of the best days of my life.
Akihabara is one of the most famous places in Tokyo.
negatives: I have one of the tickets.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with a range of determiners before a superlative adjective. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: DETERMINED_SUPERLATIVE_NP
ontology.pedagogical_hook: determiner + superlative + noun — slot any determiner before the rank
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker frames the top rank against any context

positives: I bought these clothes for my youngest brother.
Please wear your oldest clothes.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.mental_model: DENSE_TIME_INDEXICAL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: recently / immediately / eventually / finally — finer time-pointers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pinpoints the event on a more granular S-anchored line

positives: I went to the cinema with a new friend recently.
I immediately called her to see if everything was OK.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of manner adverbs and adverb phrases to modify how something happens.

ontology.mental_model: DENSE_MANNER_QUALIFICATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: carefully / gradually / properly — wider texture palette for the verb's HOW
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker expands the texture vocabulary of the action

positives: The teacher spoke slowly to the class.
He drove carefully through the storm.
negatives: She sang at the party last night.
He drives his car to work.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('near', 'far away', 'upstairs', 'downstairs') to indicate place.

ontology.mental_model: LOCATIVE_STAGING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: near / far away / upstairs / downstairs — place the event on the spatial stage
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions entities in shared physical space

positives: You can't go far away because your parents won't pay for it.
He went downstairs to find his coat.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'really really' with verbs and adjectives for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Adverb doubling signals intensification through repetition, creating a cumulative emphatic effect that amplifies the degree adverb's semantic contribution.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Double 'really' as emphatic intensifier — the learner exploits English adverb morphology by repetition to convey heightened intensity, a productive strategy even at intermediate levels.
ontology.agency_or_distance: SENDER_HIGH — the doubled form reflects the speaker's strong personal commitment to the proposition.

positives: I really really like her smile.
It was really really boring.
negatives: I really like it and I really mean it.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs ('a little', 'a bit') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity. ► determiners

ontology.mental_model: QUANTITATIVE_HEDGE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: a little / a bit — small step up from zero on the verb’s intensity dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker softens the verb’s force without abandoning it

positives: I can speak English a little now.
Could you move a bit closer, please?
negatives: She went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('therefore', 'furthermore', 'otherwise') to show a relationship between two clauses or sentences.

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_COUPLING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: therefore / furthermore / otherwise — wire two clauses with a logical link
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker binds clauses into consequence or addition

positives: You don't like cities with a lot of people, therefore I suggest a small school.
Furthermore, the rent is much cheaper there.
negatives: I went to the park yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of focusing adverbs ('particularly', 'especially') to point to or highlight something. ► adverbs: position

ontology.mental_model: FOCUS_NARROWING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: particularly / especially — spotlight one element from a presumed set
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent above others

positives: I usually read in my free time, particularly in the evenings.
I love all music, especially jazz.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs as discourse markers to organise text.  ►  adverbs: position ►  Discourse markers

ontology.mental_model: DISCOURSE_LINEARISATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: firstly / secondly / furthermore / moreover — map discourse onto ordered slots
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker arranges the text in linear progression

positives: Firstly, I advise you to visit both schools.
Secondly, consider the long-term effects.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('completely', 'obviously', 'clearly', 'actually', 'luckily', 'honestly', 'sadly', 'basically', 'obviously', 'hopefully') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.mental_model: STANCE_INTENSIFIER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / obviously / clearly / actually / luckily / honestly — dial the speaker's stance up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker takes explicit ownership of the stance

positives: I am completely sure of my answer.
It is obviously much more fun to go on vacation than stay at home.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.mental_model: CERTAINTY_GRADIENT_B1
ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — calibrate certainty at finer resolution
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: And it will probably be on TV next month!
If I were you I'd certainly choose not to go.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can modify an increasing range of adverbs with other adverbs.► adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings

ontology.mental_model: Modulating the intensity or precision of adverbs
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using adverbs to modify other adverbs for greater nuance

positives: We get along quite well.
It came out just yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'than' + a finite clause forming the second part of a comparison after a comparative adjective

ontology.mental_model: Comparing against a state of affairs
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing reality to expectations or facts

positives: I wish our schools could become better than they are.
The room seems to be bigger than it is really.
negatives: He is taller than his brother.
It costs more than ten dollars.

can_do_statement: Can use 'than' + a limited range of non-finite clauses (with -ing), forming the second part of a comparison after a comparative adjective

ontology.mental_model: Action comparison
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing two activities directly

positives: It's less complicated than going to a large school in a town.
It will be more fun than sitting at home.
negatives: I have more money than the king.
He ran faster than he ever had before.

can_do_statement: Can use '(not) as' + adjective/adverb + 'as' to introduce a clause (often with a substitute auxiliary verb) to talk about two things being equal or unequal in some way.

ontology.mental_model: Equality of state or degree
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Equating attributes with actions

positives: I will try to cover the work as much as I can.
I'm not watching T.V. as often as I did.
negatives: It is as cold as ice.
He is as tall as his father.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' + adjective + 'to'-infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: Excess preventing capability
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Excess attribute preventing an action

positives: I think you are too young to go on holiday by yourself.
He always told me that he was too busy to write a letter to me.
negatives: I am going to the store too.
There are too many people here.

guideword: FORM: 'THE SAME' (+ NOUN) + 'AS' + PRONOUN OR NOUN
can_do_statement: Can use 'the same' (+ noun) + 'as' + pronoun or noun.

ontology.mental_model: Equivalence of properties
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Stating identical properties between entities

positives: I wasn't the only one in my class, there were many others at the same level as me.
You like the same things as your friends.
negatives: I will do the same as I did before.
He arrived at the same time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so' + adjective + 'that' clause.

ontology.mental_model: Cause and effect through degree
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Degree so extreme it triggers an event

positives: I was so tired that I didn't have the strength to stand up.
I was so nervous that when the teacher talked to me, I shouted!
negatives: I did it so that you could be happy.

guideword: FORM: SENSE VERBS + 'AS IF' OR 'AS THOUGH' + FINITE CLAUSE
can_do_statement: Can use verbs of the senses + 'as if' or 'as though' + finite clause.

ontology.mental_model: Hypothetical reality through sensory perception
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Projecting an unreal scenario based on feeling

positives: I was excited and I felt as if I was a bird.
I think I will have to buy an umbrella because it looks as if it'll rain.
negatives: He acted as if he owned the place.
It seems as though they forgot about us.

can_do_statement: Can use 'do' + base form of a main verb, for emphasis or in formal contexts.

positives: Do write back and let me know all your news.
Do follow the instructions.
negatives: I do miss you very much.
Do you know where the station is?

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to make an offer or an invitation.

positives: Come and stay with us this weekend!
Come visit us after the holidays.
negatives: They come and visit us every summer.

can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with 'let me' + base form of a main verb, as a focusing device, to introduce something

positives: Let me tell you my story.
Let me explain something clearly.
negatives: She let me take her laptop.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions to introduce reasons, after a main clause.

ontology.mental_model: Establishing a causal relationship between events
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Giving reasons with 'as' or 'since'

positives: I prefer to stay home, as I have got another appointment.
We will have to cancel the trip since it is raining heavily.
negatives: I have been living here since 2010.
She works as a manager in the new company.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions ('so (that), in order that') to introduce purpose and result, after a main clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing purpose or intended result
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Purpose clauses with so that / in order that

positives: Please give me some extra exercises so that I can cover the work.
Bring your camera in order that we can take photos.
negatives: I was so tired that I fell asleep immediately.
He ordered that the doors be closed.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-finite subordinate clause with 'before' and 'after' + '-ing', before or after a main clause, to refer to time.

ontology.mental_model: Linking an action in time to a progressive action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Before/After + -ing

positives: I read them in the evening before going to bed.
We can relax after working hard at school.
negatives: I saw him before the morning meeting.
She arrived after the moving truck.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with time and date words to refer to the past.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of past temporal points or periods.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'this' past event or time.

positives: I received your letter this morning.
It happened this summer.
negatives: I will receive your letter tomorrow morning.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' after irregular plural nouns to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: They attract people's attention.
It is far from the children's school.
negatives: The dog's bone is buried here.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiner 'their'. ► noun phrases ► possessive pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: They returned to their car.
I couldn't see their faces.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('half of', 'enough of', 'none of',).► pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'half of', 'enough of', or 'none of' followed by 'the' or 'my'.

positives: You should spend half of your holiday with parents.
None of the stores had it.
negatives: You should spend half a holiday.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns ('most', 'enough', 'plenty of', 'loads of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing sufficiency, majority, or abundance for countable and uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'most', 'enough', 'plenty of', or 'loads of'.

positives: I am convinced that most people watch TV.
We will have plenty of time to buy tickets.
negatives: I am convinced that many people watch TV.
We will have a lot of time to buy tickets.

guideword: FORM: 'SO MUCH', 'TOO MUCH' WITH UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use 'so much' and 'too much' with uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so much' or 'too much' to exaggerate a lot of something.

positives: I have so much work at the moment.
My neighbours are making too much noise.
negatives: I have a lot of work.
My neighbours are making too many noises.

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'much' with uncountable things.

positives: How much television do you watch?
Do you have much time left?
negatives: How many televisions do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use quantifying determiners with uncountable nouns, often in informal and/or spoken contexts ('a little', 'a bit of' and 'a little bit of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing a small, indefinite quantity of uncountable entities in informal contexts.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a little', 'a bit of', or 'a little bit of'.

positives: We could spend a little time together.
I just watch a little bit of TV.
negatives: We could spend some time together.
I watch a lot of TV.

can_do_statement: Can use 'many' with plural nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'many' with plural things.

positives: Have you got many friends in England?
How many channels are there in Britain?
negatives: How much money do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs + particle + preposition + noun or pronoun.

ontology.mental_model: Spatial action chains mapping abstract state transitions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Think of the particle and preposition as directions the action takes.

positives: I could catch up with the work I missed after school.
They get on with each other very well.
negatives: I catch a ball when it is thrown.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.

ontology.mental_model: Directional verbs leading to target nouns
ontology.pedagogical_hook: These verbs always need their partner preposition to point at the object.

positives: Our company needs to train some staff on how to deal with the complaints.
I completely agree with your proposal.
negatives: We made a great deal today.
I will wait for you outside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there' with a range of modal verbs + 'be' + complement.

ontology.mental_model: Modal framing of existence
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a modal with 'there' lets you talk about possible or future existence.

positives: There will be flying cars and buses.
In the large school there might be a lot of people.
negatives: There is a flying car outside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'There' + 'be' + 'n’t' with countable and uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Existential negation
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating the 'be' verb shows something does not exist.

positives: There isn't any noise right now.
There weren't any people on the bus she took.
negatives: We weren't there when it happened.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of compound adjectives ('up-to-date', 'state-of-the-art')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen as glue for a single complex attribute
ontology.pedagogical_hook: two words, one label

positives: The report is up-to-date.
We use state-of-the-art technology.

can_do_statement: Can use adjective phrases to modify nouns.

ontology.mental_model: noun narrowed by a participial phrase
ontology.pedagogical_hook: which one? the one built when

positives: The cake made yesterday tasted great.
The letter sent last week arrived.

can_do_statement: Can use 'slightly' to modify comparative adjectives to a small degree.

ontology.mental_model: slightly nudges one point a hair above the other
ontology.pedagogical_hook: a hair above

positives: The price of a second-hand one was slightly cheaper.
The food of restaurant A is slightly better than that of B.

can_do_statement: Can use 'a lot' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: a lot blows the distance wide open
ontology.pedagogical_hook: blow the gap open

negatives: I have a lot of work.
positives: A bike is a lot cheaper than a car.
Don't you think it would be a lot easier for you?

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used attributively before countable and uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: much + comparative welds a ranked label onto the noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: rank the noun harder

positives: It is a much better investment than the bicycle.
What about a much cheaper hotel like the Plaza?

can_do_statement: Can use 'enough' after adjectives followed by 'to'-infinitive

ontology.mental_model: the threshold reached opens the action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: enough, so it can happen

negatives: I was lucky to be there.
She has enough money to travel.
He is too young to drive.
positives: I was lucky enough to take part in it last November.
Young people are not mature enough to decide by themselves.

can_do_statement: Can form adjective phrases with 'rather a' + adjective, often in formal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: rather a marks measured, formal assessment
ontology.pedagogical_hook: formal understatement

negatives: I would rather stay at home.
positives: Films tend to be rather a simple art.
I must confess that I'm rather a poor player.

can_do_statement: Can use the adjectives 'present', 'future', 'former' before a noun.

ontology.mental_model: TIME_QUALIFIER_ATTRIBUTIVE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: present / future / former + noun — mark an entity with its temporal qualifier attributively
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker slots an entity into its temporal slot

positives: I think we are very concerned about the present situation.
She is a former colleague of mine from the old office.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adjectives ('real', 'absolute', 'complete') before a noun to express intensity.

ontology.mental_model: DEGREE_INTENSIFIER_NAMING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: real / absolute / complete + noun — name the entity at the upper extreme of its scale
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker escalates the noun to its extreme

positives: This is a real problem and our town is becoming dangerous.
It was an absolute disaster for the team.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use the premodifer 'by far' to make a superlative adjective stronger.

ontology.mental_model: Amplifying the certainty and degree of a superlative claim
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'by far' to strongly emphasize a superlative

positives: This one is by far the most beautiful of all.
Christmas morning was by far the most exciting and happiest moment.
negatives: He went by far too quickly.

can_do_statement: Can use superlative adjectives before a noun + 'to'-infinitive. ► clauses: comparative

ontology.mental_model: Prescribing the optimal action or entity for a purpose
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combining superlatives with infinitives to give strong recommendations

positives: The easiest way to do it is to use computers.
A bicycle is perhaps the cheapest way to travel in the city.
negatives: He wants the best to win.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of manner adverbs to modify how something happpens.

ontology.mental_model: DENSE_MANNER_QUALIFICATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: seriously / completely / entirely / carefully / properly — wider texture palette for HOW
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker expands the texture vocabulary of the action

positives: She should take his warning seriously.
I read the email carefully before replying.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs and adverb phrases to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.mental_model: DENSE_TIME_INDEXICAL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: shortly / immediately / eventually / finally / currently / nowadays — finer temporal pointers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pins the event on a granular S-anchored line

positives: I look forward to hearing from you shortly.
She has recently moved to a new apartment.

can_do_statement: Can use degree adverbs to modify pronouns. ► pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Concept boundaries and set theory
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using degree to modify completeness of sets

positives: You can buy absolutely anything you like.
She said almost nothing during the meeting.
negatives: Almost all the people left early.

can_do_statement: Can use degree adverbs to modify noun phrases. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Modifying entity bounds
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Adverbs adjusting nominal precision

positives: It would be quite a formal meeting.
After all, he is almost a human.

can_do_statement: Can use 'never' in front position followed by an inverted subject (most commonly 'I') + main verb verb, to give focus.

ontology.mental_model: INVERTED_FOCUS_TRIGGER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Never + aux + I/you/we/they + verb — flip the clause around 'never' for dramatic focus
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker front-loads 'never' and rearranges the clause for emphasis

positives: Never have I seen such a realistic and impressive film before.
Never had I thought that would happen.
negatives: I never have seen such a realistic film.

can_do_statement: Can modify an adverb with a comparative structure.

ontology.mental_model: Comparing the manner or frequency of actions dynamically
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using comparative structures to modify adverbs

positives: Profits will rise even more sharply than last year.
We can search information much more quickly than before.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the same' (+ noun) + 'as' + clause.

ontology.mental_model: Equivalence of events or states
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Equating current reality with past facts

positives: Maybe I'll do the same thing as you did.
Some people say that friendship today is not the same as it used to be.
negatives: We wear the same uniform as you.
I bought the same book as my brother.

can_do_statement: Can use 'let's not' + base form of a main verb to make a suggestion.

positives: Let's not lose track of each other again!
Let's not make the situation more complicated.
negatives: He let us not participate in the race.

can_do_statement: Can use 'do not' for emphasis or in formal contexts.

positives: Do not hesitate to contact me.
Do not forget your passport.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-finite subordinate clause with 'after' + 'having/being' + '-ed' form, before a main clause, to refer to past time.

ontology.mental_model: Sequencing past events with perfect participle
ontology.pedagogical_hook: After having done...

positives: After having worked for many hours, you'll be tired.
After being given the pass, you can take pictures.
negatives: After working all day, I went home.
He arrived after having a big dinner.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' after a noun phrase with of to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: He is a friend of my father's.
I heard a story of your brother's.
negatives: He is a friend of my father.

can_do_statement: Can use 's'' after plural nouns to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: We stayed at my parents' house.
I want to study animals' behaviour.

can_do_statement: Can use 'their' before nouns to refer to a generic body or group of people expressed as a singular subject. ► generic pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: Everyone has their own opinion.
Every customer wants their product fast.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiner 'its' before nouns to refer to a singular inanimate subject or object.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: It has its own screen.
Verona is great with its buildings.

can_do_statement: Can use an adverb between the verb and the preposition.

ontology.mental_model: Adverbial disruption of verb-preposition unity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: The adverb interrupts the verb and its attached preposition to emphasize manner.

positives: I want to learn how to deal properly with them.
I hope you will look carefully at the enclosed papers.
negatives: I want to deal with them properly.
Look at the papers carefully before signing.

can_do_statement: Can use verb + preposition, where the preposition is separated from its complement.

ontology.mental_model: Dangling syntactic pointer
ontology.pedagogical_hook: In English, the preposition can be left behind at the end of the clause.

positives: Our clothes have to be clean and nice to look at.
But there is one difficulty which we should deal with.
negatives: Look at the beautiful painting on the wall.
Deal with the issue right now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there' with other verbs with modal meaning + 'be' + complement.

ontology.mental_model: Periphrastic modal framing of existence
ontology.pedagogical_hook: These verbs express necessity or future expectation of existence.

positives: I figured out that there had to be matches somewhere.
There is going to be a theatre performance.
negatives: There will be a great show tomorrow.
There are matches somewhere in the cabin.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of compound adjectives ('open-minded', 'above-mentioned', 'well-to-do', 'jaw-dropping')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen compresses a clause into a trait
ontology.pedagogical_hook: shrink the clause

positives: She is open-minded.
It was jaw-dropping.

can_do_statement: Can modify gradable adjectives with extreme adverbs of degree ('absolutely', 'extremely', 'incredibly', 'totally') to intensify their meaning.

ontology.mental_model: extreme adverbs slam the scale to its end
ontology.pedagogical_hook: slam the top of the scale

negatives: I am very sure about it.
It is quite difficult, I suppose.
positives: I am absolutely sure that it will attract even more attention.
It is extremely difficult to imagine how workers lived.

can_do_statement: Can use the '–ed' form of a verb as an adjective, after a noun.

ontology.mental_model: REDUCED_CLAUSE_BECOMES_MODIFIER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: noun + past-participle — distill a full relative clause into a compact modifier
