ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker compresses the relational structure into a property word

positives: After each film shown, the lights came up and there was applause.
The problems discussed at the meeting were resolved the next day.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a postmodifier to make the superlative stronger in the structure superlative + postmodifier + noun.

ontology.mental_model: POSTMODIFIED_TIER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the + superlative + noun + that/who/which/I/you/we — annotate the top member with a clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker appends a clause to sharpen the superlative target

positives: It was the worst decision that the committee made all year.
She's the brightest student who has ever attended this school.

can_do_statement: Can use a postmodifier to make the superlative stronger, in the structure superlative + noun + postmodifier ('possible', 'ever', 'by far').

ontology.mental_model: Maximizing the superlative scope to all available possibilities or time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Adding postmodifiers like 'possible' or 'ever' to strengthen superlatives

positives: We want to present ourselves in the best way possible.
That is her greatest performance ever.
negatives: It was her greatest performance in history.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.mental_model: WIDE_CERTAINTY_GRADIENT
ontology.pedagogical_hook: undoubtedly / undeniably / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — high end of the certainty dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks the proposition as settled

positives: It was undoubtedly an unforgettable experience.
Television programmes are undeniably a powerful influence.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of stance adverbs (simply, truly, surely, apparently, naturally, surprisingly, inevitably, literally, exceptionally, frankly, clearly, amazingly, wisely, admittedly) to indicate an attitude or viewpoint, often in clause initial position.

ontology.mental_model: REFINED_STANCE
ontology.pedagogical_hook: simply / truly / surely / apparently / naturally / surprisingly / inevitably — finer-grained stance markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks nuanced distance from the proposition

positives: Obviously everybody has the right to be on a strike.
We can't truly blame ourselves for the outcome.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs with adjectives to express degree or intensity.

ontology.mental_model: WIDE_DEGREE_CALIBRATION
ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / absolutely / extremely / totally / utterly / thoroughly — turn the adjective past every default
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pushes the adjective to the upper extreme

positives: It deals with the friendship between two completely different men.
It is extremely important to finish on time.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can post-modify adverbs with 'enough to intensify'.

ontology.mental_model: Evaluating situations as sufficiently surprising or notable
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Post-modifying adverbs with 'enough' to express attitude

positives: Surprisingly enough, management was very responsive.
Sadly enough, I wasn't able to find a job.

can_do_statement: Can modify a wide range of adverbs with other adverbs.

ontology.mental_model: Fine-tuning adverbial meaning with high-register modifiers
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Modifying adverbs extensively for precise academic or professional tone

positives: The value will drop extremely rapidly.
We can achieve market penetration relatively quickly.

can_do_statement: Can post-modify adverbs with a complex prepositional phrase complement, to highlight information.

ontology.mental_model: Highlighting the scope of an evaluative adverb using prepositional frames
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using prepositional phrases after adverbs to target specific information

positives: Luckily for you, I kept notes.
Unfortunately for some of them, it was nightmarish.
negatives: Luckily, I kept notes for you.
Unfortunately, it was bad for them.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'LET' + THIRD PERSON PRONOUN, PERMISSION, ORDER
can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with  'let' + 'him/her/them' + base form of a main verb, to  give permission or allow something or instruct someone to allow something.

positives: Let him decide what to do.
Let them have more free time.
negatives: Let us go to the park.

can_do_statement: Can use imperatives to point within or to a document within formal contexts, often academic.

positives: See enclosed brochure for further information.
Look at the graph below.
negatives: I will see you tomorrow at the office.
They looked at the picture on the wall.

can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with  'let' + 'him/her/them' + base form of a main verb, to disallow something or instruct someone to disallow something.

positives: Don't let them spend all their time playing games.
Don't let him go out alone.

can_do_statement: Can use imperatives to introduce a condition followed by 'and' to introduce a consequence of the condition.

ontology.mental_model: HYPOTHETICAL_DISTAL_REALITY
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Price Tag — hanging an automatic consequence off an order: do X, and Y follows.

positives: See one of them and you'll want to see them all.
Do that again and I'll call the police.
negatives: Try the cake and tell me what you think.

can_do_statement: Can use non-finite clauses after 'if'. .► 'clauses: conditionals'

ontology.mental_model: Abbreviating conditional states
ontology.pedagogical_hook: if + VBN or VBG

positives: Please do not hesitate to ask for further assistance if needed.
There are some suggestions that, if taken, could improve the school.
negatives: If you need anything, let me know.
I don't know if he is coming.

can_do_statement: Can use 'one's' to indicate possession, referring to people in general.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: Tourism can affect one's life.
It depends on one's ability to communicate.

can_do_statement: Can use a list of adjectives in ellipted clauses before and after a noun, to give focus. ► focus

ontology.mental_model: fronted attribute list spotlights the referent
ontology.pedagogical_hook: praise first, name second

negatives: He was imaginative, kind and friendly.
He walked in tall and dark.
positives: Imaginative, kind and friendly, he was loved.
Tall, dark and handsome, he walked in.

can_do_statement: Can combine more complex, lengthy strings of adjectives, joining the last two adjectives with 'and'.

ontology.mental_model: long attribute chain closed by and
ontology.pedagogical_hook: build the long list cleanly

positives: She is timid, shy and vulnerable.
The society is materialistic, greedy and shallow.

can_do_statement: Can use 'no' / 'not any' with comparative adjectives to limit the scale of comparison. ► comparative clauses

ontology.mental_model: no caps the scale at zero difference
ontology.pedagogical_hook: deny the gap entirely

positives: I will probably find the water to be no higher than my thighs.
They are not any happier than you were.

can_do_statement: Can use 'not that much' to modify comparative adjectives to a small degree. ► comparative clauses

ontology.mental_model: not that much shrinks the distance under scrutiny
ontology.pedagogical_hook: understate the gap

negatives: I don't have that much money.
positives: She is not that much older than I am.
The trip was not that much worse than driving.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives in 'as … as' and 'so … that' in comparative structures. ► comparative clauses

ontology.mental_model: as/so inserts the adjective between scale and article
ontology.pedagogical_hook: adjective splits as and a

negatives: He is as tall as his brother.
It was so big that we laughed.
positives: Our debates do not draw as large a number of students as the guest appearances.
He had so strong a shock that he never spoke of it.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adjectives before a noun to express intensity.

ontology.mental_model: INTENSIFIED_PROPERTY_NAMING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: intensifier + adjective + noun — push the quality word to the upper extreme before the entity
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker escalates a quality to its extreme

positives: The major problem concerns the exam.
It was a complete disaster for the team.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the slightest', 'the faintest' with a specific range of nouns to express the least amount possible, most frequently following a negative verb form.

ontology.mental_model: MARGINAL_TIER
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the slightest / the faintest + noun — name the tiniest margin of a thing

positives: I don't have the slightest idea what you mean.
There wasn't the faintest trace of evidence.
negatives: There is a faint trace of light.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs mid clause, to distance the writer from what they are saying.

ontology.mental_model: EPISTEMIC_DISTANCING
ontology.pedagogical_hook: allegedly / supposedly / reportedly / presumably — disclaim responsibility for the assertion

positives: He came out from school and supposedly joined the best university in Chile.
The witness reportedly saw the suspect run toward the station.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs in mid position, to distance the writer from what they are saying.

ontology.mental_model: EPISTEMIC_DISTANCING_MID
ontology.pedagogical_hook: allegedly / supposedly / reportedly / theoretically / arguably / presumably — slot distancing adverbs medially
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker maximum-distance from the proposition mid-clause

positives: Piggy himself theoretically has all the necessary character traits.
The witness reportedly saw the suspect run toward the station.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'hardly' in front position followed by an inverted subject and verb, to give focus.

ontology.mental_model: INVERTED_FOCUS_TRIGGER_HARDLY
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Hardly + aux + subject + verb — flip the clause around 'hardly' for dramatic foregrounding
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker front-loads 'hardly' and rearranges the clause for emphasis

positives: Hardly had he reached his front door when he heard the phone ringing.
Hardly had she finished her complaints when the bell rang.

can_do_statement: Can form adverb phrases with modifiers before, and complements after, adverbs.

ontology.mental_model: Enveloping adverbs in pre- and post-modifiers for absolute precision
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming complex adverb phrases with both preceding and following modifiers

positives: To work almost exclusively for their own interests.
It was so completely in harmony with the sun.
negatives: To work exclusively for their own interests.
It was completely in harmony with the sun.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'LET' + THIRD PERSON PRONOUN, DEVOLVING RESPONSIBILITY
can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with 'let' + 'him/her/them' + base form of a main verb, to devolve responsibility.

ontology.mental_model: DIRECT_ACTION_CONTROL
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Hands Off — withdrawing control entirely and ceding the outcome to another agent.

positives: Let them be.
Let them find their own food.
negatives: Let them have more free time.
Let him decide what to do.

can_do_statement: Can use you with an imperative form to make an instruction stronger.

positives: Don't you ever do that again!
Don't you dare forget about us!
negatives: Don't you like chocolate ice cream?

can_do_statement: Can use 'How' + clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing deep feeling or reminiscence.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'How' directly followed by a subject and verb.

positives: How I love the smell of home!
How she wishes things were different.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with nouns and noun phrases in a narrative to create a sense of immediacy.

ontology.mental_model: Creating narrative immediacy through reference to specific entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Bringing the listener into the story with 'this' character or event.

positives: There's this flame of passion between them.
There was this old man who made a marionette.
negatives: An old man made a marionette.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' and 'those' to convey emotional distance, often to express disapproval.

ontology.mental_model: Distancing oneself from a concept or behaviour.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'that' or 'those' for emotional distance or disapproval.

positives: I would never accept that sort of treatment.
Why do we listen to those so-called heroes?
negatives: I have that sort in my collection already.

guideword: FORM: SINGULAR NOUN ENDING IN 'S' + APOSTROPHE
can_do_statement: Can use an apostrophe after singular nouns ending in 's', to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: We must keep the series' aspects the same.
I drove James' car to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use two possessive ''s' constructions in the same noun phrase.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: They were in Ann's mother's albums.
We went to Emily's grandmother's house.
negatives: The cat's toy is under the dog's bed.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' without a following noun when the noun has already been mentioned or is obvious in the context.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: Olivia's experiences are probably the narrator's.
The empty account was my friend's.

guideword: FORM: VERB + DIRECT OBJECT + PARTICLE + PREPOSITION + OBJECT
can_do_statement: Can use a direct object with some prepositional verbs as well as an object of the preposition.

ontology.mental_model: Transitive split across structural bounds
ontology.pedagogical_hook: The object sits directly after the verb, splitting the verb from its particles.

positives: They can trust us or let us in on a secret.
Please don't put me up to this task.
negatives: Please let us in right now.
They decided to let us go.
